summary.en: M23 rebels have seized a major town in eastern DRC, breaching a ceasefire and intensifying fighting with the Congolese army. ADF gunmen continue killing civilians in Ituri province amid the ongoing Ebola outbreak. The Francophonie summit saw a dispute between DR Congo and Rwanda over leadership, prompting a postponement of the vote. Five European states have agreed to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda, establishing a migrant return hub there. The conflict caused 1,158 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: M23‑opprørerne har tatt kontroll over en større by i østlige DR Kongo, brutt en våpenhvile og økt kampene med den congolesiske hæren. ADF-våpnere fortsetter å drepe sivile i Ituri-provinsen mens ebolautbruddet pågår. På Francophonie-toppen oppsto en tvist mellom DR Kongo og Rwanda om lederskap, noe som førte til at avstemningen ble utsatt. Fem europeiske land har blitt enige om å sende avviste asylsøkere til Rwanda, og etablere et retur-senter for migranter der. Konflikten forårsaket 1 158 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: M23 campaign (2022–present)
background.extract: The M23 campaign is an ongoing series of military offensives launched by the March 23 Movement (M23), a Rwandan-backed rebel paramilitary group in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, since March 2022. In November 2021, M23 first launched attacks against the Congolese military (FARDC) and MONUSCO, seizing military positions in Ndiza, Cyanzu, and Runyoni in North Kivu Province. This coincided with the deployment of Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) to the region to combat the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan rebel group operating in the Congo's North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
